chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ، الصَّيْرَفِيُّ. يَرْوِي عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ). ضَعِيفٌ، مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ، لَا يُعْبَأُ بِهِ.

translations.en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sālim, al-Ṣayrafī (the money changer). He narrates from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him). Weak, a proponent of irtifāʿ in doctrine, he is insignificant.

en.summary: This entry from *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies ʿAbdullāh ibn Sālim al-Ṣayrafī as a weak narrator (*da'if*) whose specific theological flaw was an exaggerated doctrine of *irtifāʿ* (elevation), likely implying a denial of the Imams' human experiences or minor faults. In Shia hadith criticism, this elevation often signaled a tendency toward *ghuluww* (exaggeration), rendering his narrations less reliable for establishing legal or theological norms.
en.seo_question: Who is ʿAbdullāh ibn Sālim al-Ṣayrafī and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.الصَّيْرَفِيُّ: The money changer (a common kunya/nisba indicating profession)
key_terms.مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ: Proponent of irtifāʿ (believing the Imam is elevated above minor faults)
